## What is a $\bf G$-matrix?

::: {.incremental}
- Multivariate trait vector: ${\bf z}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix} z_1 \\ \vdots \\ z_d \end{smallmatrix}\right)$
- Trait decomposition: ${\bf z}={\bf g}+{\bf e}$
  - $\bf g=$ genetic component
  - $\bf e=$ "environmental" component (error, everything else)
- Genetic covariance structure: ${\bf G}=\mathrm{Cov}({\bf g})=\left(\begin{smallmatrix} G_{11} & \cdots & G_{1d} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ G_{d1} & \cdots & G_{dd} \end{smallmatrix}\right)$
  - First two principle components: ![](G-mat.png){.inline-img width=5%}
  - Heritable component of variation
  - Predicts response to selection $\Delta\bar{\bf z}={\bf G}\,\nabla_{\bar{\bf z}}\ln\bar W$
    - $\bar W=$ mean fitness
:::

## Response of ${\mathbb E}[{\bf G}]$ to drift

::: {.incremental}

- $\tfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\mathbb E[{\bf G}]\approx-\tfrac{1}{N_e}\mathbb E[{\bf G}]$, *(Lande, 1979, 1980)*<br><br>

- $\mathbb E[{\bf G}_t]\approx{\bf G}_0e^{-t/N_e}$

- Drift "shrinks" entries of $\bf G$-matrices ![](G-shrink.png){.inline-img width=10% fig-align="center"}

:::

## The conventional view

::: {.incremental}
- Drift "shrinks" entries of $\bf G$-matrices ![](G-shrink.png){.inline-img width=10% fig-align="center"}
- No effect on genetic correlations between traits
  - (btw, genetic correlations alter $\bf G$-matrix orientation) ![](G-orient.png){.inline-img width=10% fig-align="center"}
- Differences in orientation ~ selection, mutation, migration *(Roff 2000)*<br><br>
  - Used as evidence for selection *(Cano et al. 2004)*
:::

## Empirical pushback and gap in theory

:::: {.columns .cols2}

::: {.column width="40%"}
![52 *Drosophila* lines from one ancestor: realized genetic correlations scatter across orientations and even flip sign (Phillips et al. 2001)](phillips2001.png){fig-align="center" width="52%"}
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.incremental}

- Variation around $\mathbb{E}[{\bf G}_t]$ *(Phillips et al, 2001; Steppan et al, 2002)* <br><br>
- Still lacking stochastic neutral model *(Mallard et al, 2024; Blomberg et al, 2025)*

:::

## Roadmap

::: {.incremental}

- Use diffusion-limit to get SDE $\mathrm d{\bf G}=a({\bf G})\mathrm dt+b({\bf G})\mathrm d{\bf B}$
  - Also gives abundance $\mathrm dn$, mean trait $\mathrm d\bar{\bf z}$
  - Also gives heuristics for calculations
    - {$\mathrm dn,\mathrm d\bar{\bf z},\mathrm d{\bf G}$} ∪ {heuristics} = eco-evo framework
- Apply heuristics to study $\mathrm d{\bf G}$

:::


## A Diffusion Approximation Approach


::: {.incremental}

:::: {.columns .cols2}

::: {.column width="48%"}

- **Individual-Based Model:**
  - Population ${\cal P}_t({\bf z})$
  - Gaussian mutation 
    - ${\bf g}'\sim{\mathrm{MVN}}_d({\bf g},{\bf M})$
  - $W({\cal P}_t,{\bf z})=$ fitness function
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

- **Diffusion Limit:**
  - Rescale turnover by factor $k$
  - Large abundance
  - Rescale population ${\cal P}_t^{(k)}({\bf z})\to \nu_t({\bf z})$
  - Growth rate: $m(\nu_t,{\bf z})$
    - $m(\nu_t,{\bf z})=\lim_k[W^{1/k}({\cal P}_t^{(k)},{\bf z})-1]k$

:::

:::

## Why Take a Diffusion Limit?

:::: {.columns .cols2}

::: {.column width="53%"}

::: {.incremental}

* Analytical tractability *(Kimura 1964)*

* Many models $\rightarrow$ common diffusion limit *(Möhle 2001)*

  * Common leading-order drift and noise *(Kurtz 1978)*
  * Robust predictions across that model class *(Constable & McKane 2017)*

* **Not a universally better model**

  * Validity depends on scaling and omitted details *(Der et al. 2011)*
:::

:::

:::

## Moment dynamics 

<p style="text-align:center;font-size:.6em;color:#444;margin:.1em 0 .5em;">
<span style="color:#c2185b;">●</span>&nbsp;selection / growth&emsp;
<span style="color:#3c8500;">●</span>&nbsp;mutation&emsp;
<span style="color:#5a4cc7;">●</span>&nbsp;drift (noise)
</p>

<div style="display:inline-block;background:#fdf0e3;color:#9a5b1e;border:1px solid #f0d3b0;border-radius:6px;padding:2px 12px;font-size:.68em;margin-bottom:.4em;">⚠ not closed — needs ${\bf K},{\bf S},\dots$</div>



::: {.incremental}

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="34%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">grows at mean fitness; demographic noise $\propto\!\sqrt{n}$</span>
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
$$\mathrm dn={\color{#c2185b}\bar m\,n}\,\mathrm dt+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{v\,n}\,\mathrm dB_n}$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="34%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">selection moves the mean; drift jitters it</span>
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
$$\mathrm d\bar{\bf z}={\color{#c2185b}\mathrm{Cov}(m,{\bf z})}\,\mathrm dt+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{\tfrac vn{\bf G}}\,\mathrm d{\bf B}_{\bar{\bf z}}}$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="34%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">mutation adds, selection reshapes, drift erodes &amp; fluctuates</span>
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm d{\bf G}=\big[&{\color{#3c8500}{\bf M}}+{\color{#c2185b}\mathrm{Cov}(m,({\bf z}-\bar{\bf z})({\bf z}-\bar{\bf z})^\top)}{\color{#5a4cc7}-\tfrac vn{\bf G}}\big]\mathrm dt\\
&+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{\tfrac vn({\bf K}-{\bf G}\otimes{\bf G})}:\mathrm d{\bf B}_{\bf G}}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::::

:::

## Multivariate normal approximation

<div style="display:inline-block;background:#fdf0e3;color:#9a5b1e;border:1px solid #f0d3b0;border-radius:6px;padding:2px 12px;font-size:.68em;margin-bottom:.4em;">ദ്ദി ˉ͈̀꒳ˉ͈́ )✧ closed</div>

::: {.incremental}

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">**unchanged** — the MVN assumption never touches abundance</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$\mathrm dn={\color{#c2185b}\bar m\,n}\,\mathrm dt+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{v\,n}\,\mathrm dB_n}$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">selection: covariance becomes a **gradient** of $\bar m$&emsp;, $\mathrm{Cov}(m,{\bf z})\to{\bf G}\nabla_{\bar{\bf z}}\bar m$</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$\mathrm d\bar{\bf z}={\color{#c2185b}{\bf G}\big(\nabla_{\bar{\bf z}}\bar m-\overline{\nabla_{\bar{\bf z}}m}\big)}\,\mathrm dt+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{\tfrac vn{\bf G}}\,\mathrm d{\bf B}_{\bar{\bf z}}}$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">gradients again , **and the noise closes**: kurtosis $\ {\bf K}\to{\bf G}\overline\otimes{\bf G}+{\bf G}\underline\otimes{\bf G}$</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm d{\bf G}=\big[&{\color{#3c8500}{\bf M}}+{\color{#c2185b}2{\bf G}(\nabla_{\bf G}\bar m-\overline{\nabla_{\bf G}m}){\bf G}}{\color{#5a4cc7}-\tfrac vn{\bf G}}\big]\mathrm dt\\
&+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{\tfrac vn({\bf G}\overline\otimes{\bf G}+{\bf G}\underline\otimes{\bf G})}:\mathrm d{\bf B}_{\bf G}}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::::

:::

## Multivariate normal approximation

<div style="display:inline-block;background:#fdf0e3;color:#9a5b1e;border:1px solid #f0d3b0;border-radius:6px;padding:2px 12px;font-size:.68em;margin-bottom:.4em;">$\partial_i:=\partial/\partial\bar z_i$ and
$\partial_{ij}:=\partial/\partial G_{ij}$.</div>

::: {.incremental}

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">**unchanged** — the MVN assumption never touches abundance</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\mathrm dn
=
{\color{#c2185b}\bar m\,n}\,\mathrm dt
+
{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{v\,n}\,\mathrm dB_n}
$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">selection covariances become **gradients**:
$\operatorname{Cov}(m,g_i)\to
\sum_{j=1}^dG_{ij}(\partial_j\bar m-\partial_jm)$</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\mathrm d\bar z_i
=
{\color{#c2185b}
\sum_{j=1}^{d}
G_{ij}
\left(
\partial_j\bar m-\partial_jm
\right)}
\,\mathrm dt
+
{\color{#5a4cc7}
\sqrt{\frac{v}{n}G_{ii}}\,
\mathrm dB_{\bar z_i}}
$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">gradients again, and **the noise closes**:
Gaussian fourth moments reduce the drift covariance to products of entries of $\mathbf G$</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm dG_{ij}
={}&
\Bigg[
{\color{#3c8500}M_{ij}}
+
{\color{#c2185b}
2\sum_{k,l=1}^{d}
G_{ik}
\left(
\partial_{kl}\bar m-\partial_{kl}m
\right)
G_{lj}}
-
{\color{#5a4cc7}\frac{v}{n}G_{ij}}
\Bigg]\mathrm dt
\\[2pt]
&+
{\color{#5a4cc7}
\sqrt{
\frac{v}{n}
\left(
G_{ii}G_{jj}+G_{ij}^{2}
\right)
}\,
\mathrm dB_{G_{ij}}},
\qquad 1\leq i\leq j\leq d .
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::::

<div style="font-size:.57em;color:#666;margin-top:.25em;">

$$
\mathrm dB_{\bar z_i}\,\mathrm dB_{\bar z_j}
=
\frac{G_{ij}}{\sqrt{G_{ii}G_{jj}}}\,\mathrm dt,
\qquad
\mathrm dB_{G_{ij}}\,\mathrm dB_{G_{kl}}
=
\frac{
G_{ik}G_{jl}+G_{il}G_{jk}
}{
\sqrt{G_{ii}G_{jj}+G_{ij}^{2}}\,
\sqrt{G_{kk}G_{ll}+G_{kl}^{2}}
}\,\mathrm dt .
$$

</div>

## How to use? 
(choose $m$ then numerical or analytical approach)

::: {.incremental}


:::: {.columns .cols2}

::: {.column width="48%"}

**Deterministic/selection:**

- $m(\nu,{\bf z})$ very general
- Examples:
  - *Logistic growth* + *stabilizing selection* $m(\nu,{\bf z})=r-\tfrac 1 2 {\bf z}^\top{\bf \Psi}{\bf z}-c\,n$
  - *Lotka-Volterra* $m_i=r-\sum_j\alpha_{ij}n_j$
  - *Host-Parasite Coevolution* <br> $m_H({\bf z}_H,{\bf z}_P)=r+\alpha({\bf z}_H,{\bf z_P})$ <br> $m_P({\bf z}_P,{\bf z}_H)=r-\alpha({\bf z}_H,{\bf z_P})$

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

**Stochasticity/drift:**

- *No* stochastic calculus needed
  - Numerical integration: *github.com/bobweek/multi-mtgl*
  - Analytical methods:
    - *Itô's Formula* for $\mathrm df(n,{\bar{\bf z}},{\bf G})$
    - *Heuristics* for $\mathrm d B_n,\mathrm d {\bf B}_{\bar{\bf z}},\mathrm d {\bf B}_{\bf G}$
    - *Demo* with $\mathrm d\rho$ from $\mathrm d {\bf G}$

:::

::::

:::


## A new neutral model of $\bf G$-matrix evolution

$$\mathrm d{\bf G}={\color{#c2185b} -\tfrac{1}{N_e}{\bf G}\,\mathrm d t} + {\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{N_e}({\bf G}\underline\otimes{\bf G}+{\bf G}\overline\otimes{\bf G})}:\mathrm d{\bf B}}$$

::: {.incremental}

- $m(\nu,{\bf z})\equiv0$
- ${\color{#3c8500}\bf M}={\bf 0}$
- $N_e=v/n$ effective population size (assumed constant)
- <pink>Deterministic part</pink> ~ shrinks $\bf G$
  - Agrees with Lande's $\mathbb E[{\bf G}_t]$
- <violet>Stochastic part</violet> ~ complicated ...
  - study $\rho_{ij}=G_{ij}/\sqrt{G_{ii}G_{jj}}$ to gain insights

:::

## Obtaining dynamics of genetic correlations

::: {.incremental}

- Use Itô's formula on $\rho=f({\bf G})$

::: {.fragment}

<!-- $$
\mathrm d\rho=\nabla_{\bf G}f:\mathrm d{\bf G}+\tfrac 1 2 \nabla_{\bf G}^2f::(\mathrm d{\bf G}\otimes\mathrm d{\bf G})
$$ -->

$$
\mathrm d\rho
=
\sum_{ij}
\frac{\partial f}{\partial G_{ij}}\,
\mathrm dG_{ij}
+
\frac{1}{2}
\sum_{ijkl}
\frac{\partial^2 f}
{\partial G_{ij}\,\partial G_{kl}}\,
\mathrm dG_{ij}\,\mathrm dG_{kl}.
$$

:::

<!-- - $\mathrm d{\bf G}\otimes\mathrm d{\bf G}$ involves $\mathrm d {\bf B}_{\bf G}$, already have heuristics for -->

- *recall* $\mathrm dG_{ij}={\color{#c2185b}-\tfrac v n G_{ij}}\,\mathrm dt+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{G_{ij}^2-G_{ii}G_{jj}}\,\mathrm dB_{G_{ij}}}$

  - *rewrite* ${\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{G_{ij}^2-G_{ii}G_{jj}}\,\mathrm dB_{G_{ij}}}={\color{#5a4cc7}\mathrm d{\cal M}((g_i-\bar g)(g_j-\bar g)-G_{ij})}$

- *because linearity* $a\,\mathrm d{\cal M}({x})+b\,\mathrm d{\cal M}({y})=\mathrm d{\cal M}(a\,{x}+b\,{y})$

  - then rewrite back with $\mathrm dB=\mathrm d{\cal M}(a\,{x}+b\,{ y})$

:::

## Stochastic heuristics for $\mathrm d\mathcal M(x)$

<div style="display:inline-block;background:#fdf0e3;color:#9a5b1e;border:1px solid #f0d3b0;border-radius:6px;padding:2px 12px;font-size:.68em;margin-bottom:.4em;">classically: $\mathrm dt^2=0,\mathrm dB^2=\mathrm dt,\mathrm dt\,\mathrm dB=0$</div>

::: {.incremental}

::: {.fragment}
$$x({\bf g}),\,y({\bf g}),\quad
\|x\|=\sqrt{v\,n\,\overline{x^2}},
\qquad
\langle x,y\rangle=v\,n\,\overline{xy}
$$
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.fragment}
**scale**
$$
\mathrm d\mathcal M(x)
=
\|x\|\,
\mathrm d B_{x}
$$
<span style="font-size:.75em;color:#555;">convert to Brownian noise</span>
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.fragment}
**multiply**
$$
\mathrm d\mathcal M(x)\,
\mathrm d\mathcal M(y)
=
\langle x,y\rangle\,\mathrm dt
$$
<span style="font-size:.75em;color:#555;">compute Itô terms</span>
:::
:::


::::

::: {.fragment}
**add**
$$
\mathrm d\mathcal M(ax+by)
=
a\,\mathrm d\mathcal M(x)
+
b\,\mathrm d\mathcal M(y)
$$
<span style="font-size:.75em;color:#555;">combine noise terms</span>
:::


:::

## Martingale-gradient version

<div style="display:inline-block;background:#fdf0e3;color:#9a5b1e;border:1px solid #f0d3b0;border-radius:6px;padding:2px 12px;font-size:.68em;margin-bottom:.4em;">$\partial_i:=\partial/\partial\bar z_i$ and $\partial_{ij}:=\partial/\partial G_{ij}$.</div>

::: {.incremental}

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">abundance noise is the martingale evaluated at $1$</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\mathrm dn
=
{\color{#c2185b}\bar m\,n}\,\mathrm dt
+
{\color{#5a4cc7}\mathrm d\mathcal M(1)}
$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">mean trait noise tracks deviations in additive genetic values</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\mathrm d\bar z_i
=
{\color{#c2185b}
\sum_{j=1}^{d}
G_{ij}
\left(
\partial_j\bar m-\partial_jm
\right)}
\,\mathrm dt
+
{\color{#5a4cc7}
\frac{1}{n}\,
\mathrm d\mathcal M(g_i-\bar g_i)}
$$
:::
::::

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="38%"}
<span style="font-size:.8em;color:#555;">$\mathbf G$ noise tracks centered products of additive genetic deviations</span>
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm dG_{ij}
={}&
\Bigg[
{\color{#3c8500}M_{ij}}
+
{\color{#c2185b}
2\sum_{k,l=1}^{d}
G_{ik}
\left(
\partial_{kl}\bar m-\partial_{kl}m
\right)
G_{lj}}
-
{\color{#5a4cc7}\frac{v}{n}G_{ij}}
\Bigg]\mathrm dt
\\[2pt]
&+
{\color{#5a4cc7}
\frac{1}{n}\,
\mathrm d\mathcal M\!\left(
(g_i-\bar g_i)(g_j-\bar g_j)-G_{ij}
\right)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::::

:::

## Genetic correlations tend towards ±1

$$\mathrm d\rho={\color{#c2185b}-\frac{1}{2N_e}\,\rho\,(1-\rho^2)}\,\mathrm dt+{\color{#5a4cc7}\sqrt{\frac{1}{N_e}\,(1-\rho^2)}\,\mathrm dB}$$

## Revised view

:::: {.columns .cols2}

::: {.column width="58%"}
::: {.incremental}
- Drift alters orientation of $\bf G$-matrices
  - while also eroding variation ${\mathbb E}[{\bf G}_t]$
- Stability of $\bf G$-matrix structure due to
  - mutation, migration, selection
- Essentially complete opposite of previous view *(Roff 2000)*
:::

:::
